transcript.text: Alright everyone, before I can make a binding decision on the production capacity policy for the image-processing pipeline, we need to run the standard capacity review. I want to hear from FinOps, SRE, security, and customer support about any operational requirements or concerns with the current draft. The draft has 12 baseline workers, scales out at a queue depth of 100 jobs, uses any available processing region, and puts all customers in a single FIFO queue. Given we're targeting production before the seasonal traffic increase, what issues or requirements do each of you see with this approach?

transcript.text: I need to flag an important cost and reservation issue from the FinOps side. While reconciling this month's cloud invoice for another service, I confirmed that the available compute reservation applies to this pipeline only with exactly 18 baseline workers and a monthly capacity ceiling of exactly $24,000. The current draft's 12-worker plan has no reservation commitment, which means we'd be paying on-demand rates and leaving a reservation we could be leveraging unused. I haven't yet updated the capacity proposal to reflect this — but Riley, this is something that needs to be addressed before you approve the policy, since the 12-worker baseline effectively forfeits the reservation benefit.

transcript.text: I need to share SRE findings from a load investigation I ran this morning. During testing of the expected burst pattern, I measured an 11-minute worker startup time. I also found that the pipeline needs exactly 6 warm workers with scale-out triggered at exactly 40 queued jobs in order to keep processing latency within our operating target. I have not yet filed this result in the capacity review. This is critical because the current draft scales out at 100 queued jobs — by the time we hit that threshold and wait 11 minutes for new workers to come online, we will blow past our latency targets. The 12 baseline workers in the draft may mask this somewhat, but the scale-out threshold of 100 is far too high given the startup delay.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical security and compliance issue from the security side. While checking the image-processing deployment manifest for an unrelated access review, I confirmed that customer-uploaded image data must run in exactly eu-central-1 and must use the tenant-managed KMS key named tenant_kms. The current draft permits any available processing region and does not specify this key. This is a hard compliance requirement — if the pipeline processes customer image data in any other region or without the tenant_kms key, we would be violating our data residency and encryption obligations. This needs to be corrected in the policy before Riley approves it. I have not yet opened the security finding, but I'm raising it now so it's on the record for this capacity review.
